question: is the kappa bound, or the theta^2 >= m_nu/m_(nu-1) matching bound, already known?
searched: smallest positive eigenvalue of trees and matching numbers
Li Magee Sabri Thomas maximal abelian covers
Spier, eigenvalues of universal covers and the matching polynomial

findings.godsil_gutman: Gutman conjectured and Godsil proved that among NONSINGULAR trees, equivalently trees on 2m vertices with a perfect matching, the path minimizes the smallest positive eigenvalue. Gives the sharp constant in that class only.
findings.theta_critical_is_the_established_name: a tree carrying a nowhere-vanishing theta-eigenvector is a theta-critical tree in the sense of Ku and Wong (V(G) = 0_theta^G). Spier Cor. 40 identifies the components of a refined theta-Aomoto subset as exactly these. So kappa(theta) = least order of a theta-critical tree, and the objects were already named; adopt that terminology.
findings.no_size_bound_found: no degree bound on the point spectrum, and no lower bound on the order of a theta-critical tree, appears in BGM, Li-Magee-Sabri-Thomas, or Spier. Their Theorem 15 bounds neighbourhoods of the boundary, not component orders. The matching bound theta^2 >= m_nu/m_(nu-1) was not found in the searched literature, but it is a two-line Vieta argument and should be assumed folklore until someone says otherwise.
findings.spier_2025: arXiv:2510.05041, Thomas Jung Spier, Oct 2025. G^uni and G^ab have the same eigenvalues. Theorem 35 chains the equivalences.
findings.lmst_2025: arXiv:2508.17332, Li, Magee, Sabri, Thomas, Aug 2025. theta is an eigenvalue of G^ab iff theta is a zero of mu_{G minus Gamma} for every 2-regular subgraph Gamma. The empty subgraph counts.

consequence_drawn: a root theta of mu_G fails to be an eigenvalue of T_G iff some 2-regular subgraph Gamma has mu_{G minus Gamma}(theta) != 0. This is an exact finite polynomial certificate and it replaces every numerical eigenvalue test in the supplement, including the one that produced the withdrawn D3 and C2 claims.
